newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Women's ranges boost Austin Reed.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Women's ranges boost Austin Reed.

text.p: Austin Reed Group Plc, purveyors of British business fashion around the world, said on Wednesday its first-half profits were boosted by an upturn in consumer confidence and a bounce back in sales of its women's ranges.
The U.K.-based retailer and manufacturer saw first-half pre-tax profits jump 64 percent to 2.3 million stg while sales climbed seven percent to 38.9 million stg.
The company's new management team said there are encouraging signs of an upturn in consumer spending in the U.K. and predicted further "steady progress" in the second half.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, chief executive Chris Thomson said "it is clear that there's been a relaxation of consumer spending, but I wouldn't describe it as a boom. We are trading in a very competitive market."
Austin Reed said its autumn retail sales are ahead by around nine percent from a year before.

Thomson said the turnaround in sales of womens' clothing, which account for around 20 percent of the total, has been particularly notable following a "bit of a disaster" in the spring of 1995 when Austin Reed's ranges "didn't sell and we had to substantially discount to get rid of stock."

Thomson said the management team at Austin Reed, which includes a new retail division managing director, finance director and chief executive, had no plans to alter the balance of sales between men's and women's clothing, but added "we need to be alert to opportunities."
The company plans to increase business in the competitive European market, stepping up sales of its branded clothing through German, French and Italian retailers in particular.
"The Austin Reed brand is well known in Europe, being a quintessentially British brand, and I think there are tremendous opportunities to expand that," Thomson said.
Austin Reed is also committed to licensing its name to manufacturers in the U.S. and Japan, another important source of income.
Thomson said that despite the upturn in consumer spending, profit margins continue to be "highly fought for," while the group's cost base "continues too improve."

Austin Reed is looking to expand its U.K. retail base of around 50 stores, with new outlets in the heart of London's financial district, a new shopping centre in Dartford and the upmarket Manchester dormitory town of Wilmslow all in its sights.
